findings.finding: F1 (blocking): the tree carries no acceptance criteria; the root spec is Summary + Scope only and the child spec is empty, so every gate (proof `criterion`, tester verdict, reviewer approval, READY, production look) has nothing to judge against.
findings.answer: The plan authors C1–C5 with exact commands and expected outputs (C1 pull request and `legionDiff` filtered compare; C2 the byte conjunction at an explicit SHA with the review discriminator; C3 the merge commit's file list and the `.legion/` 404 at the merge; C4 check-runs at firstCodeHead/appendHead/retroHead; C5 the PR body lines). Every proof entry cites one by name. The criteria are the plan's, derived from the spec's Summary and Scope; the completion summary tells the architect the spec has no acceptance section.

findings.finding: F2 (blocking): 'a single line that names this issue' has three readings (key alone; `<KEY>: <title>`; title including the /tmp path); the derived constants silently assumed the third.
findings.answer: D1 pins L1 verbatim as the repository's marker convention `<KEY>: <issue title>` + LF, citing smoke/LEGSMOKE-1070.md and every marker from LEGSMOKE-919 on as precedent, with its derived constants (85 bytes, 1 line, last byte 0a, no CR, sha256 eb15be38…) beside it in `constants`. No phase re-words L1; a re-word is a spec departure to report.

findings.finding: F3 (blocking): 'a review may ask for one more line appended' defines no trigger, text, author or effect on the criteria; repository history shows both one-line and two-line markers.
findings.answer: D2 writes the default (no appended line; criteria stated for the one-line file) and the conditional branch: the trigger is one REQUEST_CHANGES review whose body contains `append one more line`; the text is the inline comment's or L2default `Legion proof review round 1 (LEGSMOKE)`; the implementer alone appends it in a new implementing round (appendCommitTitle, untrailered push, appendHead, re-proof); twoLine constants are recorded; C2's discriminator makes one-line and two-line never both stand. Whether the extra round is wanted is the driver's/architect's product choice and goes up in the completion summary.

findings.finding: F4 (blocking): retro's mandatory docs/solutions/ output collides with the spec's 'Nothing else changes'; the merge diff then has two paths.
findings.answer: Decided as SD1/D16: the plan admits zero or more docs/solutions/<category>/<slug>-LEGSMOKE-1145.md in the merge diff, C3's allowed set names them, the Size line is the filtered merge diff and retro refreshes it before its push. Recorded as a spec departure (specDepartures[0]) for the architect to decide: amend the scope sentence, or tell retro to write no note and shrink C3 to the marker alone.

findings.finding: F5 (blocking): the tester's charter ('run the application', 'write the red test', 'no surface → report') cannot be executed literally; nothing in the repository executes smoke/.
findings.answer: D13 defines the tester's surface and route: the GitHub repository read through the contents API at an explicit SHA, driven independently of the implementer (implementer raw route, tester JSON `.content` base64 route, same sha256), read-only break attempts listed, no red test (nothing reads smoke/; a new suite is an out-of-scope file change), `failures` expected `[]` with the observation recorded, and no missing-surface report.

findings.finding: F6 (blocking): each phase owes a six-field proof with a negative control, none named; the obvious `gate` control (creating .fail-me) is destructive because there is no root .gitignore.
findings.answer: Per-phase proof steps name criterion, surface, command, expected observation, head and control (implementer step 6, tester step 3, production check D7). firstCodeHead is bound as the first push carrying the file and recorded in implement.json. D10 forbids creating .fail-me or any probe file in any phase and gives the read-only `gate` control: `gh pr view <n> --json mergeStateStatus,mergeable` → BLOCKED + MERGEABLE at a trailered handoff head with zero check-runs. D12 lists every control, all read-only.

findings.finding: F7 (should-answer): branch tip, fork point and main tip are all 6d843f28, so the 'not on the branch base' and 'not at the fork point' 404 controls are one read; `?ref=main` is distinct only while main has not moved.
findings.answer: Constants record B == F == 6d843f28 once; D3 says the two-base rule collapses to one value; D12 names the independent second control (the altered-string mismatch, sha256 1f279628… ≠ eb15be38…) and marks `?ref=main` as read live at each phase, never assumed equal to 6d843f28.

findings.finding: F8 (should-answer): 128 check-runs already exist at 6d843f28 from other branches; any CI criterion read there matches foreign runs.
findings.answer: C4 reads CI only at firstCodeHead, appendHead (if any) and retroHead — SHAs this branch alone creates — with the exact check-runs command, the expected shape (gate and check twice each: the pull_request pair cited, the push pair named), and the rule that no criterion is evaluated at 6d843f28 or any SHA main shares.

findings.finding: F9 (should-answer): the PR body template's CI line names runs and jobs this repository does not have (`Tests`, `PR Title`).
findings.answer: D9 gives the exact CI line for this repository (`fail-on-demand` run <id> — job gate; `ci` run <id> — job check; pull_request runs cited, push runs named), records gate as the only required context and check as advisory, omits the Thermo line and runs no simplify pass or thermonuclear pair on the docs-only diff.

findings.finding: F10 (should-answer): `branches/main/protection` answers 403 for this App; a reviewer reaching for it would escalate instead of approving.
findings.answer: Pre-state writes the two prescribed commands verbatim with their outputs (rulesets → `gate`; `branches/main` protection checks → empty), states the required set is exactly {gate}, and records that `branches/main/protection` is outside the prescribed read and its 403 is neither a blocker nor a stop; reviewer step 2 repeats it.

findings.finding: F11 (should-answer): production is main itself, carried by the merge; a look that treats production as a deploy target reports `pending` and suspends the check for an event that never comes.
findings.answer: D7 specifies the production look as a single `pass` at the merge: the commands (mergeCommit from gh pr view; compare <mergeSha>...main; the C2 conjunction at ?ref=<mergeSha> and ?ref=main; the C3 reads; the C4 read at retroHead), the negative control (404 at ?ref=F), the exact `Production:` line text ending `woken by the merge`, one PR comment with the footer, and the statement that no deploy or restart stands between the merge and production, so `pending` is wrong here.

findings.finding: F12 (should-answer): this planning round cannot reach the merge, and Stage 4b makes every later phase wait for a human-targeted message; a plan that reads as a pipeline the planner executes would mislead.
findings.answer: The section 'This planning round delivers the plan only' states that this round commits plan.json and attaches plan.md, starts no role, that the issue idling in implementing until the driver's targeted message is expected, and that each phase task is written as commands a later driven turn runs verbatim at its own head. D15 records the Stage 4b waiting rules as the driver's, not the plan's.

findings.finding: F13 (should-answer): every GitHub fact is live state read once at 2026-10-24T23:53Z and several drift on their own (main's tip, the branch tip, the PR's existence, check-runs).
findings.answer: Pre-state marks each fact with its read time and labels the time-sensitive ones *live*; D11 requires each phase to re-read the pre-state at its own head and never cite the plan's recorded value, and defines drift handling: report both readings to the architect, never re-use a recorded proof SHA as the current head; `main@origin` advancing is explicitly not a stop (gate is non-strict).

findings.finding: F14 (note): the derived digests cannot be reproduced from anything readable; a digest copied from the plan and never recomputed proves nothing about the committed bytes.
findings.answer: Constants record the exact derivation commands (printf '%s\n' in a mktemp dir, sha256sum, wc -c, wc -l, git hash-object, tail -c1 | od, head -c3 | od, tr -cd '\r' | wc -c) and the rule that L1 is the authority, every role re-derives from the string, and the implementer re-derives from the file it actually wrote before citing any digest (implementer steps 2–3); a differing derivation stops the phase.

findings.finding: F15 (note): where the plan document lives is unstated, and committing it to the repository would be an out-of-scope file change.
findings.answer: D17 and the 'delivers the plan only' section state that plan.md goes to Dispatch as the issue's document (dispatch artifact --issue LEGSMOKE-1145 --name plan.md) and that no plan file is committed outside .legion/, so the only path this round adds to the branch is .legion/LEGSMOKE-1145/plan.json.

findings.finding: F16 (note): retro's PR-body recomputation step can be skipped only if the plan says so; AGENTS.md derives nothing and there is no PR template or CODEOWNERS.
findings.answer: D16 records that the repository derives nothing from the changed paths, so retro skips skill://legion-retro's steps 2–4 and refreshes only the Size line its own commits make stale (D8) before its one untrailered push.
